texts: good. the when-clause turns into a rule that can actually fire — every burning of mire-essence by a lantern gives that same lantern a producing of mist-light — and "the lantern" in the main clause correctly refers back to the lantern in the condition.
good. the whenever version fires the same way, with "gives" recorded as a handing-over rather than a making, which is what the wording says.
good. mist-light is recorded as a flame, as a light, as pale and as silver; the only nuance flattened is that "pale" shades "silver" rather than standing beside it, and nothing you stated is dropped.
good. the denial becomes a rule that reaches any particular ordinary oil, with "ordinary" kept as the condition, so the reasoner can rule out mist-light for a specific oil.
